pr.title: Add a scheme for moving away from `extern "rust-intrinsic"` entirely
pr.description:
All `rust-intrinsic`s can become free functions now, either with a fallback body, or with a dummy body and an attribute, requiring backends to actually implement the intrinsic.

This PR demonstrates the dummy-body scheme with the `vtable_size` intrinsic.

cc https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/63585

follow-up to #120500

MCP at https://github.com/rust-lang/compiler-team/issues/720
pr.author: oli-obk

analysis.originalLogic: The `intrinsic` query returned `Option<Symbol>` and classified a definition as an intrinsic when its ABI was `RustIntrinsic` or it had `#[rustc_intrinsic]`. `LowerIntrinsics` matched on that symbol to replace calls with MIR operations (`&& let Some(intrinsic) = tcx.intrinsic(def_id)` then `match intrinsic.name`), and `InstSimplify` resolved calls to `(intrinsic.name, args)`. If a call was not lowered or simplified, codegen could fall back to the definition as an ordinary function/body.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Representing intrinsic identity by name alone and assuming every intrinsic has a usable fallback body. For an intrinsic declared with a dummy body but marked as requiring backend implementation, a pass/codegen path could leave the call to be handled as a normal function, or encode/export/inline its MIR, thereby silently using the placeholder body instead of forcing backend lowering or an error. The corrected model carries `IntrinsicDef { name, must_be_overridden }` and all body-using paths reject or skip such definitions.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust/MIR definitions declared via legacy `extern "rust-intrinsic"` or `#[rustc_intrinsic]`, optionally annotated `#[rustc_intrinsic_must_be_overridden]`, with either a real fallback body or a dummy body (`unreachable!()`, `panic!()`, `loop {}`, or an empty body), together with reachable call sites whose callee type is `ty::FnDef(def_id, args)`.
analysis.summary: Intrinsic identity is more than a name: a dummy-bodied `#[rustc_intrinsic]` that backends must override needs a `must_be_overridden` flag so MIR passes, MIR encoding/inlining, symbol export, and codegen never fall back to executing its placeholder body. `LowerIntrinsics` and `InstSimplify` must consume the richer intrinsic query and only replace calls when they have a real lowering/simplification; otherwise the backend must implement the intrinsic or report an error.
analysis.trigger: A reachable call to a definition recognized by `tcx.intrinsic(def_id)` where the intrinsic has a dummy/fallback body and may be annotated `#[rustc_intrinsic_must_be_overridden]`; passes such as `LowerIntrinsics`/`InstSimplify` or codegen must decide whether to lower, simplify, or defer to the backend.
preconditions: The callee type is `ty::FnDef(def_id, _)` and `tcx.intrinsic(def_id)` returns `Some`, as in `LowerIntrinsics`'s `let Some(intrinsic) = tcx.intrinsic(def_id)` and `InstSimplify`'s `tcx.intrinsic(def_id)?`.
The definition is a `DefKind::Fn` or `DefKind::AssocFn`; the query now returns `None` for other definition kinds.
`must_be_overridden` is true only when the definition has `#[rustc_intrinsic_must_be_overridden]`; the dummy body exists only to satisfy type checking and must not be used.
For intrinsics that `LowerIntrinsics` replaces with MIR operations, the body is irrelevant after MIR analyses because calls to the intrinsic no longer exist.
pitfalls: Matching only on the intrinsic name loses whether the body is usable; `must_be_overridden` must travel with the intrinsic identity.

Do not assume every `#[rustc_intrinsic]` is marked `must_be_overridden`: the run-pass test intentionally declares `vtable_size` without that attribute and still expects the backend to override the panic body.

Checking the raw attribute in hot paths creates HIR depgraph edges; the PR replaces `has_attr(..., sym::rustc_intrinsic_must_be_overridden)` with `tcx.intrinsic(def_id).is_some_and(|i| i.must_be_overridden)`.
The query is now legal for any `DefId`, so callers must handle `None` for non-function definitions instead of assuming a function.
A missing backend implementation for a `must_be_overridden` intrinsic is a compiler error, not a reason to fall back to `Instance::new` or to encode/inline/export the dummy MIR.
analysis.testStrategy: Use paired Rust UI tests that differ only in the intrinsic marker and expected outcome. First, a run-pass test declaring `#[rustc_intrinsic] pub unsafe fn vtable_size(_ptr: *const ()) -> usize { panic!(); }` without `#[rustc_intrinsic_must_be_overridden]`, calling it through a trait-object vtable, and asserting the backend-provided size (`0`). Second, a build-fail test declaring `#[rustc_intrinsic] #[rustc_intrinsic_must_be_overridden] pub const unsafe fn const_deallocate(...) {}` and calling it, expecting a diagnostic containing `must be overridden by codegen backend, but isn't` rather than silently executing the empty body. For pass-level verification, inspect MIR before/after `LowerIntrinsics`/`InstSimplify`; do not claim compiler execution or reproduction.
